headline: Growth beats guidance; full-year outlook raised again
summary_short: Revenue rose 14.9% y/y to $1,310M in Q2 2026 (10% organic constant currency) and net income climbed 30.8% to $143M; TransUnion raised its full-year 2026 guidance to 12%-13% revenue growth and $4.75-$4.83 adjusted diluted EPS.
summary_long: Revenue grew 15% y/y (10% organic constant currency) as U.S. Financial Services (+18%) benefited from FICO mortgage royalty pricing and volume, while International jumped 27% on the Trans Union de Mexico acquisition and Canada/U.K. growth, partly offset by weaker Consumer Interactive and Asia Pacific. Adjusted EBITDA rose 12% to $456M though margin fell 90bp on higher FICO royalty costs. Net income rose 31% y/y to $143M; a sequential decline from Q1 reflects Q1's one-time $225.5M non-taxable Mexico-acquisition gain, not a deterioration. Cash was $839M, net debt $4.75B (2.6x leverage). TransUnion raised full-year 2026 guidance to 12%-13% revenue growth and $4.75-$4.83 adjusted diluted EPS.

drivers.explanation: U.S. Markets Financial Services grew 18% on FICO mortgage royalty pricing and volume; International grew 27%, driven by the Trans Union de Mexico acquisition in Latin America and broad-based volume gains in Canada and the U.K.
Operating income rose $65.8M as revenue growth outpaced cost growth, partly offset by higher interest expense from debt used to fund the Trans Union de Mexico acquisition.

Higher revenue and continued transformation-plan cost savings drove the increase, partially offset by higher product costs, primarily FICO mortgage royalties in U.S. Markets; the same royalty cost also compressed margin 90bp.
Adjusted Net Income improved on better operating performance, partially offset by higher net interest expense and a higher adjusted tax provision from increased pre-tax income.

Sequential (q/q) net income and EPS look like a steep decline only because Q1 2026 booked a one-time $225.5M non-taxable gain on the Mexico acquisition and a much lower 13.1% H1 tax rate; Q2's 27.2% rate is the representative run-rate.
